stayRegimes.title: 30-day visa exemption for Dutch passports
stayRegimes.note: A return or onward ticket is required.

stayRegimes.title: 240-hour visa-free transit
stayRegimes.note: Needs an onward ticket to a third country and a passport valid for more than 3 months. Fuzhou and Xiamen airports qualify; confirm other ports with the National Immigration Administration.

stayRegimes.title: 45-day visa exemption
stayRegimes.suggestWhenTooLong: Apply for an e-visa (up to 90 days) — only at evisa.gov.vn or thithucdientu.gov.vn; ignore paid lookalike sites.
stayRegimes.note: Treat it as non-extendable. Needs a return or onward ticket and proof of the trip's purpose.

stayRegimes.title: Visa-free stay
stayRegimes.note: You must be able to show you'll leave Thailand within this period.

stayRegimes.title: Lao e-visa
stayRegimes.note: Check the stay on your approval letter.

stayRegimes.title: Lao visa on arrival
stayRegimes.note: Check the date stamped in your passport.

stayRegimes.title: Visa-free stay
stayRegimes.note: Longer stays: extend at the Bureau of Immigration before the 30 days run out. After 6 months an ECC is needed to leave.

onward.why: China wants to see a return or onward ticket.
Vietnam's visa exemption needs a return or onward ticket.
Thailand wants proof that you'll leave within the visa-free period.
onward.weakProofNote: A local bus paid on board proves nothing at the border. Keep other proof ready: your Laos e-visa plus the flight out of Laos, or a pre-booked bus or boat into Laos.

onward.why: The Philippines checks your exit ticket on arrival.

evisa.processing: about 3 working days; 4×6 cm photo and passport bio page; fee via the official calculator

ports.name: Boten checkpoint and Boten railway station

forms.name: China online arrival card
forms.detail: Only via the official site, the NIA 12367 app or the WeChat/Alipay mini-programs. Fill it in before travelling; paper cards on arrival are the fallback.

forms.name: Visit Japan Web
forms.detail: Recommended: one QR code covers immigration and customs. Save a screenshot of it; paper forms are still accepted.

forms.name: Vietnam pre-arrival form
forms.entryPointMatch: \b(HAN|SGN|DAD|PQC)\b|noi bai|tan son nhat|ho chi minh|hanoi|da nang|phu quoc
forms.detail: Mandatory when landing at Ho Chi Minh City, Hanoi, Da Nang or Phu Quoc.

forms.name: Thailand Digital Arrival Card (TDAC)
forms.detail: Free, for air and land arrivals, within 3 days before arrival. Only at tdac.immigration.go.th — ignore paid lookalike sites. It's done at the first Thai airport, also on a connection.

forms.name: Laos Digital Immigration Form (arrival)
forms.detail: Within 3 days before arrival. Keep the QR code offline.

forms.name: Laos Digital Immigration Form (departure)
forms.detail: Again within 3 days before leaving Laos. Keep the QR code offline.

forms.name: eTravel (arrival)
forms.detail: Free, within 72 hours before arrival; the QR code is shown at check-in. Ignore paid lookalike sites.

forms.name: eTravel (departure)
forms.detail: The Dutch advice says to fill it in before departure too.

bookingWindows.name: Laos–China Railway
bookingWindows.detail: Domestic tickets go on sale about 7 days ahead at 06:30 Laos time in the official LCR Ticket app and sell out fast in December–February. Some travellers need a Lao, Thai or Chinese phone number to register. Station security bans aerosols and knives.

advisoryAreas.detail: The Golden Triangle lies on the Myanmar border, where a 10 km strip is orange in the Dutch advice (the towns of Mae Sai, Mae Sot and Ranong excepted). Check the map in the live advice and what your policy says.

Huay Xai is in Bokeo province, where the Laos–Myanmar border area is orange in the Dutch advice. Check on the map that Huay Xai and the Gibbon Experience area are outside it, and what your policy says.
Xaysomboune province is orange in the Dutch advice.
Parts of western Mindanao, the Sulu archipelago and the Sulu Sea are red in the Dutch advice.
South-east Fukushima has a red zone (the nuclear exclusion area).

bag.title: Vapes are banned
bag.detail: Bringing, using or selling vapes and refills is banned — Vietnam: heavy fines or 1–15 years in prison; Thailand: up to 10 years; Laos: vapes and shisha banned. Leave them at home.

bag.title: E-liquid limit in Japan
bag.detail: Maximum 120 ml of e-cigarette liquid per month for personal use.

bag.title: Medicines into Japan
bag.detail: Up to one month's supply of ordinary prescription medicine (two months over-the-counter) without paperwork; more needs an Import Confirmation applied for online before arrival. Amphetamine-type ADHD medicine is prohibited; some substances (e.g. lisdexamfetamine, pseudoephedrine) are controlled.

bag.title: Scooters in Vietnam
bag.detail: Many tourist accidents. The Dutch advice: only ride under 50 cc, have an IDP, and make sure your insurance covers vehicle accidents.

bag.title: Diving needs extra cover
bag.detail: Check your policy's diving cover and maximum depth.

holidays.name: Culture Day
holidays.detail: National holiday: busier transport, some offices closed.

holidays.name: Rizal Day and New Year
holidays.detail: Holidays: full ferries and flights, closed offices.

holidays.name: Sinulog festival
holidays.detail: Third Sunday of January in Cebu: fully booked hotels and busy transport.

crossings.name: Friendship Bridge IV (Chiang Khong ↔ Huay Xai)
crossings.requirements: Lao visa on arrival: per traveller guides bring a passport photo and US dollars (the cheapest way to pay); a small overtime fee applies after 16:00 and at weekends and holidays.
crossings.howToCross: From Chiang Rai's central bus terminal a local bus leaves towards Chiang Khong about every hour (~2 h, ~90 THB paid on board). Ask for the Laos border and take a tuk-tuk to the bridge. The bridge can only be crossed by the shuttle bus (small fee, no walking), then a tuk-tuk into Huay Xai.

driving.detail: A Dutch licence is only valid together with an IDP of the 1949 model. The ANWB issues it in person at its stores (bring your licence, proof of address and a passport photo; you get it on the spot), so arrange it before leaving the Netherlands.
The Dutch advice: only ride under 50 cc, have an IDP, and make sure insurance covers vehicle accidents.
An IDP is required; it is valid for at most 90 days.
The Dutch advice: a Dutch licence is only valid together with a valid IDP.
The Dutch advice: a Dutch licence is not valid in China, not even with an IDP; you need a local Chinese licence.

The Dutch advice: almost all scooters in Thailand count as motorbikes. Without a valid (international) motorcycle licence your travel insurance often won't pay. Never hand over your passport or licence as a deposit.
